term: all-premise generated inferential warrant versus epistemic justification
definition: A Justification supplies rule tokens, each rule’s full premise predicate and conclusion, a noninferential foundation predicate, and an independent justified predicate. GeneratedWarrant is inductively generated by noninferential foundations and application of a rule whose every premise has GeneratedWarrant. The inferential graph projects premise membership to a rule conclusion; one projected edge never certifies sufficiency. Path extraction additionally requires every inferential rule to have a premise, so zero-premise rules cannot silently replace foundations. The extracted path is a necessary condition only, not a sufficiency theorem or a claim that all possible justification is foundationalist.
note: A stipulated foundationalist standard, not attributed to Agrippa, Sextus, or any contemporary epistemologist. Epistemic justification, positive knowledge, logical satisfiability, modal possibility, ontological existence and actual causal power are distinct. No automatic bridge relates them. Historical attribution would require a pinned and materialized passage defending these foundation and rule clauses; applying the norm to real justification would additionally require an independent argument.
